clue.text: That flowery Miss

parts.note: reads as a young lady with a flower's first name who comes from the dales, but it names a spring bloom

explanation.surface: Pointing out a young woman with a fondness for florid language.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant is a woodland flower with a girl's name as its first word, so it could be a Miss from a dale.

clue.text: By which one may well be lugged off.

definitions.text: By which one may well be lugged off.

parts.words: By which one may well be lugged off
parts.note: to be lugged is to be hauled along, and 'lug' is also slang for an ear, so these are the soft parts a person is dragged off by

explanation.surface: A remark about how someone gets hauled away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lug' is British slang for an ear; a naughty child is dragged away by the soft lower parts of the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleshy hanging parts of the ears are what an angry adult grabs to tow a child.

clue.text: Strange liana suit from old Roman in Spain.

indicators.note: something strange is out of its normal form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tropical creeper and a suit of clothes oddly traced back to an ancient Iberian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges LIANASUIT. The definition is a Roman province of the Iberian peninsula, roughly modern Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the Roman province covering the western Iberian peninsula, a Roman region of Hispania.

clue.text: Half a dozen deliveries — a thing of the

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Half a dozen deliveries — a thing of the (4)', is cut short: the second definition ('a thing of the past') lacks its last word and there is no scan.
annotationWithheld.clue: Half a dozen deliveries — a thing of the

clue.text: Mostly rational, this crime against government.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Mostly rational, this crime against government. (7)', gives no parse: 'Mostly rational' yields no letters that with anything else build the answer; likely garbled OCR.
annotationWithheld.clue: Mostly rational, this crime against government.

clue.text: "In all the — round you tread. Th nothing but the night." (Housman.)

definitions.text: "In all the — round you tread. Th nothing but the night." (Housman.)

parts.words: "In all the — round you tread. Th nothing but the night." (Housman.)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from A. E. Housman's poem: the missing word describes a road that never stops

explanation.surface: A line of verse by the poet A. E. Housman with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem's lines are 'In all the endless road you tread / There's nothing but the night'; the OCR has garbled some words but the gap is clear.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank is filled by an adjective meaning without a stop, from Housman's verse.

clue.text: Nicer coat perhaps as an outside addition.

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the given words are only one possible arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a better coat might serve as an extra layer outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Accretion is growth by layers gathering on the outside, a build-up added from without.

clue.text: Bloodsucking witch in a mail rig- 1

indicators.note: to rig something is to arrange it falsely, so these letters are fixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A vampire-like witch dressed up in chain-mail gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rig' rearranges AMAIL; the clue's tail has been garbled in printing but the anagram is plain.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical myth she is a female monster who drinks the blood of children and young men.

clue.text: One of those that Macbeth said lighted fools the way to dusty death.

definitions.text: One of those that Macbeth said lighted fools the way to dusty death.

parts.words: One of those that Macbeth said lighted fools the way to dusty death
parts.note: Macbeth's speech says 'all our ... have lighted fools the way to dusty death', and the clue asks for one of those past days

explanation.surface: A reference to Macbeth's famous lament on the futility of life.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Shakespeare's 'Tomorrow, and tomorrow, and tomorrow' speech: 'And all our yesterdays have lighted fools / The way to dusty death.'
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth's speech names past days as having lit fools towards the grave; one such is the day before today.

clue.text: Make an unwelcome investment,

parts.note: reads as a bad financial stake, but to invest a town is an old military sense meaning to surround it

explanation.surface: Putting money into something nobody wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' in the military sense is the encircling of a fortress, which its defenders hardly welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: To surround a town with troops is a siege, the military investment of a place.

clue.text: Folds one's tents like the Arabs?

definitions.text: Folds one's tents like the Arabs?

parts.words: Folds one's tents like the Arabs
parts.note: alludes to Longfellow's line about folding tents like the Arabs and silently stealing away

explanation.surface: A nomad packing up the camp before moving on.
explanation.walkthrough: Longfellow wrote 'shall fold their tents, like the Arabs, / And as silently steal away'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack up camp and leave, often hurriedly, is to break camp and go.

clue.text: Dangerous item disclosing the situation

indicators.note: disclosing means the two words reveal a run of letters lurking across their join

explanation.surface: A hazardous object revealing where things stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A location or position where something is placed, as with a building plot.

clue.text: The donkey kept on eating, so to speak.

parts.note: a donkey is an ass
kept on means always or continually, ever
eating gives the past tense 'ate', loosely, as in had a meal

explanation.surface: A donkey that would not stop chewing, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to' is a link; the definition is the verb at the end, used here for a solemn declaration.
explanation.definitionFit: To asseverate is to declare or state earnestly, a formal way to say something.

clue.text: House, but you must see no man is about.

indicators.note: about means the words are turned around and reordered

explanation.surface: A Donne-like reminder that nobody is an island, applied to a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges NOMANIS; the surface echoes John Donne's 'No man is an island'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large stately dwelling is a grand kind of residence.

clue.text: It causes a fine flare-up.

parts.note: suggests a quarrel, but means a metal that burns with a brilliant white light

explanation.surface: Something that sparks off a splendid row.
explanation.walkthrough: The metal burns with a dazzling white flame, used in flares and old photographic flashes.
explanation.definitionFit: This light metallic element ignites with an intense white flame, hence its use in flares.

clue.text: Afternoon party at Poona ?

parts.note: Poona is a city in India, so a tea party held there is a subcontinental one; the answer is also a kind of brew

explanation.surface: A colonial-era gathering for cakes and sandwiches in India.
explanation.walkthrough: Poona (now Pune) was a British Raj hill station; the phrase is also the name of a type of tea leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea party at Poona is literally a subcontinental tea, which is also the name of black tea grown there.

clue.text: The pit's about to finish, but there's pay.

indicators.note: about means the word is turned round to face the other way

parts.note: taken as the plural of pit
to finish means to end

explanation.surface: A mine is about to close but the wages are still coming.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed regular salary, especially a clergyman's, is a payment.

clue.text: Skilled performer, not, one hopes, with an'ax

definitions.text: Skilled performer, not, one hopes, with an'ax

parts.words: Skilled performer, not, one hopes, with an'ax
parts.note: a skilled performer, whose title begins like the word for putting someone to death with an axe

explanation.surface: A virtuoso who, we trust, does not wield a hatchet.
explanation.walkthrough: The word looks like a cousin of 'execute' in the beheading sense, hence the axe.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer, especially a skilled musician, who carries out a piece of music.

clue.text: Wary, a statement like this.

explanation.surface: Describing a cautious person and their carefully hedged remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Wary means cautious; a non-committal statement is likewise careful, saying little.

clue.text: One way to run down.

parts.note: running someone down means belittling them; one way to do it is to take away from their merit

explanation.surface: A suggestion of one method for running down a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: To belittle or take away from someone's worth is to disparage them.

clue.text: Where to apply if you are wanting

definitions.text: Where to apply if you are wanting

parts.words: Where to apply if you are wanting
parts.note: reads as a job office for the needy, but someone wanting a tin would go to the factory that makes or fills them

explanation.surface: Advice on where to seek help when in need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' suggests poverty; here it means wanting a tin, for a factory that preserves food in tins.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory where food is sealed in tins is where the tins are filled.

clue.text: Stick together after starting on French leave,

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Stick together after starting on French leave, (7)', gives CONGE (French leave) but nothing for the final AL; the clue appears cut short in OCR.
annotationWithheld.clue: Stick together after starting on French leave,

clue.text: Could one call it an essential process?

definitions.text: Could one call it an essential process?

parts.words: Could one call it an essential process
parts.note: an essential process is one that draws out an essence, as in distilling oils

explanation.surface: Asking whether something is a vital procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essential' means of essences: drawing out an essence from a plant is the process meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing out an essence or juice is removing it, the process for essences.

clue.text: Just an intermediate word in short.

definitions.text: Just an intermediate word in short.

parts.words: Just an intermediate word in short
parts.note: a word meaning in the middle of two things, cut short with an apostrophe

explanation.surface: A small connecting word, briefly put.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the poetic short form of 'between'.
explanation.definitionFit: The clipped poetic form of a preposition meaning in the middle of two things.

clue.text: An act to divert you.

explanation.surface: A stage performance meant to entertain the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety performer's act is a spot on the bill; to divert is to send in another direction.

clue.text: Nicely flavoured, but not all there?

explanation.surface: Something tasty but a little crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasting richly of nuts, and, informally, slightly mad or eccentric.

clue.text: Likely part of a castle to last.

explanation.surface: A stronghold built to endure.
explanation.definitionFit: The central fortified tower of a castle; also, to remain good or endure.

clue.text: Quite the wrong mood for getting on.

definitions.text: Quite the wrong mood for getting on.

parts.words: Quite the wrong mood for getting on
parts.note: getting on means making progress, and a state of sluggish unwillingness to move is no help with it

explanation.surface: A bad frame of mind for succeeding in life.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a tendency to stay at rest, the reluctance to move or act.

clue.text: Having that polished look.

parts.note: polished in the sense of refined and stylish rather than buffed to a shine

explanation.surface: Something shining as if waxed.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceful and stylish in appearance is refined, smart and polished.

clue.text: Mind the communication in this case!

definitions.text: Mind the communication in this case!

parts.words: Mind the communication in this case
parts.note: reads as a warning to take care, but here 'mind' is the medium through which the message passes

explanation.surface: A warning to be careful about a message.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing thoughts directly from one mind to another, without speech, is thought transfer.
